subject: Dedicated reservation sizing Q&A and throughput calibration
messages:

Cc: Kevin Lee <kevin.lee@orioncloud.io>

Subject: RFP: Dedicated inference reservation — clarification on throughput/GPUs

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the RFP response packet — nice detail. A couple of clarifying items from procurement and infra before we complete our internal sizing:

- We need a mapping from model types (open LLM variants) to recommended GPU families for both steady-state and burst windows.
- Can you provide realistic examples: e.g., what a 500 reqs/min generation workload (avg 400 tokens per request) would look like in terms of "# GPUs baseline" and "# GPUs burst"?
- What assumptions are you making about batching, KV cache reuse and tokenization overhead?
- Any constraints on colocating embeddings traffic vs generation?

Attached: our RFP (short). Happy to take a short workshop if useful.

Also looping Kevin from our cloud ops — they want to understand how reservation and burst lanes would interact with our private VPC setup.

Best,
Maya Rivera
Head of Procurement, AcmeCorp

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kevin Lee <kevin.lee@orioncloud.io>
Date: Mon, 2 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated inference reservation — clarification on throughput/GPUs

Thanks Maya — appreciate the clear asks. I pulled together an initial workbook with conservative baseline and burst scenarios (attached). Quick answers up-front:

- We recommend a mixed fleet approach: H100-family nodes for heavy-generation (large-context, high token rates) and A100-80 for mid-sized models/embedding-heavy lanes. For ultra-cost-sensitive embedding-only workloads we can suggest A10 or triton-optimized quantized variants.
- Example capacity: for 500 reqs/min with avg 400 tokens/request (generation-heavy): baseline ~6 H100s (with batching + KV reuse) and burst lane up to 10 H100s (30–40% burst headroom). That assumes p95 gen latency target ~1.2s for 400-token outputs.
- Assumptions: 50–80 token batch size, persistent KV cache for repeated sessions, 8-bit quantization for eligible models. We call these out in the workbook so you can toggle parameters.

Can we schedule a 45-min workshop this week so Marissa (solutions) and Alex (infra) can walk the workbook and align GPU mix to your anticipated model mix? I attached the workbook and a quick-fit CSV for our recommended GPU fit.

Karthik
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing-workbook.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 72KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 May 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated inference reservation — technical calibration notes

Karthik / Alex — added more concrete tech assumptions and a recommended packing approach. Notes below (feel free to copy these into the workbook before sending):

1) Model to GPU guidance (starter recommendation)
   - Small/embedding-only (up to 2B): A10 / T4 family, quantized; use shared embedding pool to reduce tail.
   - Medium generation (7B–13B): A100-80GB, batched; good cost/throughput for seq <= 1024.
   - Large generation (34B+): H100-family (80GB) recommended for consistent latency at long context lengths and for larger kv-cache requirements.

2) Throughput examples (empirical baselines we use in sizing calculations)
   - H100-80GB: for a 34B-ish model, with batch size 16 and seq len 512, sustained generation throughput ~3,500–5,000 tokens/sec per GPU depending on kernel/quantization.
   - A100-80GB: for 13B with batch 32, sustained ~6,000–9,000 tokens/sec per GPU for quantized runtimes.
   - Embedding endpoints: a single A100 can handle many tens of thousands of small embedding requests per minute when batched; treat them as separate lanes for reservation planning.

3) Reservation planning rules of thumb
   - Baseline = expected 95th percentile sustained load over a 30-day window.
   - Burst buffer = +30–50% of baseline for predictable day/time peaks; allow auto-burst into a shared pool or hosted fallback for unexpected surges.
   - If your workload has long-lived conversations (KV reuse), size baseline smaller; KV cache reduces repeated compute significantly.

4) Example worked scenario (your ask: 500 req/min @ 400 tokens)
   - Tokens/min = 500 * 400 = 200,000 tokens/min => ~3,333 tokens/sec.
   - If we assume H100 yields 4,000 tokens/sec (conservative median), baseline H100s = ceil(3,333 / 4,000) = 1 (but we apply utilization headroom). For production with p95 latency SLO, we recommend baseline 4 H100s with burst to 8–10 for headroom + scheduling inefficiencies and maintenance.
   - Alternatively, mixed fleet: 2 H100 + 6 A100-80 as a cost-optimized blend depending on model mix.

5) Co-location note
   - Keep embedding traffic on separate GPU pool or partitioned queues. Embeddings have tiny per-request cost but high qps; colocating with generation increases tail and scheduling complexity.

Attachments I added: "gpu-fit-matrix.csv" with per-GPU throughput bands and "redwood-dedicated-sizing-workbook.xlsx" (you already have). I also sketched a reservation policy: baseline reservation + scheduled auto-scale windows and a warm standby pool.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: gpu-fit-matrix.csv (CSV, 6KB)]
